patch_description: Replace the random guess with a direct stochastic optimization of the target ratio dmin/dmax. Since the metric is exactly (dmin/dmax)^2, we optimize that ratio directly with a greedy random-perturbation hill-climb over many restarts (random starts plus structured starts from an icosahedron-based configuration), keeping the best configuration found. Pairwise distance computations for 14 points are cheap (91 pairs), so tens of thousands of proposals fit easily in the time budget. Hill-climbing on the true objective is far more reliable than penalized or surrogate objectives here.
